input.quote: 20.2 Vendor shall also defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the Customer indemnified parties from third-party claims to the extent arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by Vendor; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.
input.rationale: Section 20 sits at (indeed above) our preferred position, so no redline is warranted. § 20.1 gives an express Vendor duty to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel against third-party claims that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate IP. § 20.2 extends the Vendor indemnity to Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud. § 20.4 supplies the standard procedure — prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, and control of the defence (with a materiality-of-prejudice carve-out and a settlement-consent protection favouring us). Customer's reciprocal indemnity in § 20.3 is properly narrow: unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized, plus Customer's violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions. The fallback remedy ladder is also present in § 20.5 (procure, modify or replace, else terminate and refund prepaid and implementation Fees), and the fallback's 3× super-cap is unnecessary because § 21.3 treats indemnification obligations, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud and IP infringement as Excluded Claims outside the § 21.1 cap — i.e. uncapped, which is better for us. The only sub-preferred points are cosmetic and are noted rather than flagged: the refund is on a straight-line three-year basis, and § 20.5's exclusions for Customer modifications/combinations/specifications are addressed structurally (through the "to the extent" allocation and § 20.3) rather than as an express exclusion list — neither is a material shortfall and neither disadvantages us.
